content.body:
Made famous by the Flying Tigers of the American Volunteer Group (AVG) in China, the Hawk H81A-2 was neither a P-40B nor a P-40C, but actually a kind of hybrid.
USAAF orders had already shifted to the D and E models of the P-40 when the war broke out, and the H81 was seen by Curtiss managers as a potential cash cow for the company as an export fighter. While not the best in speed or climb above low/med altitudes, its rugged construction, good maneuverability, and incredible dive performance made it a very attractive buy for France as the war drew closer. An order was placed and filled, but when shipped to France the ports were shut down at Cherbourg and Le Touquet at the fall of French authority in the spring of 1940, just as the aircraft were due to be delivered to the French Air Force. Because they were actually just offshore at the time, they were quickly re-routed to England and the RAF.
Unique in the Curtiss P-40 line, the H81 was faster than a P-40B and lighter than a P-40C.
With a decent gun arrangement of two .50 cal machineguns in the nose and four .30 cals in the wings, the H81 could do well in lower altitude fights where its performance profile was at its best. Higher up, where the thinner air began to starve out the Allison engine, the Hawk 81's performance dropped considerably. Use the H81's fantastic rate of roll and its speed down low to disrupt Axis support aircraft.
You can turn and burn with the 109s down low though, and unless they climb away, you might eventually win an angles fight against them.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor MAX. SPEED: 570 km/h WEIGHT: 3,322 kg CREW: 1 ARMAMENT: .50 cal Browning M2 HMGs (2) .303 cal Browning LMGs (4)
content.title: Curtiss Hawk H81A-2
